posts.quote: I BENT DOWN FOR ONE SOCK. MY KNEE NEGOTIATED. THE SOCK IS STAYING WHERE IT IS.
posts.caption: The sock has been there since the weekend. I walk around it the way you walk around a sleeping dog. At first I told myself it was a priority problem, and that I'd get to it when things calmed down. Things have not calmed down. Yesterday I put the other sock next to it so it wouldn't be lonely. That isn't a plan, but it's a home. It might be the most organized thing I've done all week.
posts.first: I did try the grabber tool from the kitchen drawer. It picked up the sock, then dropped it somewhere worse. I've left them both. The hallway has a theme now.

posts.quote: I CHECKED THE WEATHER TO SEE IF I HAD PLANS. THE FORECAST SAID RAIN. I'VE NEVER FELT SO SUPPORTED.
posts.caption: It started with a text asking if I was free later. I told them I'd see how the day went, which is what I say when I know exactly how the day will go. Then I opened the weather app like I was checking the stock market. Rain, all afternoon, seventy percent. I sat back and let the forecast make the decision for me. Nobody has to know I was hoping. The rain has taken the blame, and it's handling it well.
posts.first: I texted back that it looked rough out there and I wouldn't want anyone driving in that. It was drizzling by four. I'd have said the same thing if it was sunny, but this was easier.

posts.quote: I OPENED THE BOX OF CHRISTMAS LIGHTS TO CHECK THEM EARLY. THEY'RE EXACTLY AS TANGLED AS I LEFT THEM. I RESPECT THE CONSISTENCY.
posts.caption: Every year I wrap them neatly in January. I put them away with care and a little speech about next year's me. Next year's me opens the box and finds a knot the size of a cantaloupe. I don't know who is doing this. The house has been quiet and the cat seems unbothered. It's either a ghost or my own two hands. I've decided it's a ghost, and I'm taking the knot to the couch to work on it.
posts.first: I got one strand loose by 9:40 and the tree is in the other room. I'm calling it a phase. The knot and I are on speaking terms now.

posts.quote: I WATERED THE PLANTS AND TOLD THEM ABOUT MY DAY. THEY LISTEN BETTER THAN SOME PEOPLE I'VE HAD DINNER WITH.
posts.caption: It started with the fern in the kitchen window. I said good morning because it looked like it needed to hear it. By the end of the week I was giving it updates. The fern doesn't interrupt. The pothos has never once checked its phone while I was talking. The ficus drops a leaf now and then, but I take that as a sign of deep feeling. They're mostly conversations about the weather and my knees. The plants are very supportive.
posts.first: Yesterday I moved the pothos closer to the chair so I wouldn't have to raise my voice. It's the best conversation I had before noon. The ficus dropped another leaf when I got to my sister.

posts.quote: I LAY DOWN FOR A TWO-MINUTE REST. IT'S NOW DARK. THE DAY MOVED ON WITHOUT ME.
posts.caption: There was a plan. I'd put the laundry in, open the mail, and be productive by noon. I sat down first, just to look at the list. The list looked back. I closed my eyes for what I'd call a blink, and when I opened them the light in the room had changed and a cat was on my chest like a paperweight. The laundry is still in the washer. It's making a point. I haven't looked at it directly since.
posts.first: The mail is where I left it on the counter, mostly bills and one thing from the county I'm not ready for. I'm treating the nap as emergency maintenance. The cat has not moved, so I'm going with that.
